 Splash Financial’s straightforward process can save borrowers and their families a lot of time finding and securing private student loans. Amy DeYoung, Special to USA TODAY Sun, 8 November 2026 at 8:27 am GMT-7 11 min read College costs are on the rise , and many students and their families are taking out private student loans to supplement scholarships and federal aid. Private student loans are a common way to bridge the gap between savings, scholarships and federal loans, but interest rates, repayment terms and loan requirements vary by lender. 
 Splash Financial is a well-known personal loan marketplace that helps borrowers pre-qualify for multiple loans through its partner lenders. Here's how the marketplace works and whether it makes sense to use, based on average repayment terms, interest rates and eligibility requirements. 
 Splash Financial overview 
 Splash Financial is a personal loan marketplace that shows you loans you qualify for through its partner lenders. This provider advertises competitive and sometimes exclusive interest rates from its lenders, along with a quick application process that reduces the hassle of shopping around different lenders or refinancing. Founded in 2013, it began by helping borrowers refinance their student loans and then expanded into guiding borrowers through taking out student, personal, auto and home equity loans. 
 Splash Financial at a glance

 Find your student loan on Splash 
 Student loan options 
 Undergraduate loans 
 Loans through Splash Financial's partner lenders can cover up to 100% of your school costs minus any scholarships or financial aid you've received. Splash lenders offer fixed and variable interest rates and standard student loan repayment options, including repayment terms of five to 20 years and the option to defer payments until after graduation. 
 Graduate loans 
 Splash Financial can help you find a lender for graduate school , including medical, dental, law and MBA programs. Some of these loans offer special benefits, including extended grace periods (up to 9 months), skip-a-payment bonuses (once a year) and no origination, prepayment or extra payment fees. 
 Story continues Student loan refinancing 
 If you're out of school and looking for a better interest rate, Splash Financial can help you compare student loan refinancing options. Splash Financial lenders have their own minimum loan amount requirements for student loan refinancing. In most cases, the minimum is $5,000. From there, you can choose between Splash's lending partners and the different fixed and variable rates and repayment terms available. 
 Splash offers special benefits for medical school loan refinancing, including advertised deals like paying just $100 a month during training and for the following six months. 
 Pro tip: Refinancing your student loans can lower your interest rate and simplify repayment. However, be cautious about refinancing federal student loans, as you can lose certain benefits, like federal repayment plans and forgiveness programs, if you opt to refinance federal loans. 
 Learn more: I refinanced my student loans. Here's how I knew it was worth it 
 Interest rates, fees and discounts 
 Fixed vs. variable rates 
 When shopping for a lender through Splash Financial, you can choose between a fixed or variable interest rate. A fixed rate stays the same while you pay off your student loan, but a variable rate changes with market conditions. 
 As of writing this, Splash Financial offers fixed rates ranging from 1.99% to 17.99 and variable rates ranging from 4.64% to 15.99%. Student loan refinancing starts at a 4.29% fixed APR and 4.74% variable APR, but goes up to 11.37% APR for each. 
 Available discounts 
 Certain Splash lending partners offer an autopay discount, which usually lowers your rate by 0.25%. The autopay discount lets the lender withdraw your monthly loan payment from your bank account each month. 
 Fees 
 In many cases, Splash doesn't charge an origination fee, but keep an eye out, as its terms and conditions state it can charge up to a 15% origination fee (depending on loan type and lender). 
 Compared to other lending marketplaces, up to 15% is steep. 
 Splash doesn't charge an application fee to apply for or view rates. However, late fees depend on the lender you choose, so always read each lender's terms and conditions before you decide. 
 Repayment options 
 Once you've selected a private student loan, you'll want to review that specific lender's repayment options and terms closely. Terms vary by lender, but most give borrowers five to 20 years to pay the loan back. 
 In-school repayment options 
 Private student loan borrowers can opt for different in-school repayment options, depending on the Splash partner lender. 
 Interest-only: Some lenders let borrowers pay only the interest while in school. 
 Flat monthly payments: This option lets you pay $25 per month toward your loan while you're in school, which can help reduce interest and build the habit of paying off your student loans. 
 Immediate repayment: If you opt for immediate repayment, you'll make complete principal and interest payments while in school. 
 Deferred repayment: This repayment option means you don't make any payments while in school and for a grace period following graduation (typically around six months). 
 Repayment term lengths 
 For most loans, you can choose between five, eight, 10 or 15 years, although certain graduate student loans allow up to 20 years for the loan's lifetime. 
 Grace period 
 A grace period is the time after graduation or leaving school before you must start making monthly payments on your student loan. Most Splash lenders have a standard 6-month grace period, but some graduate students may receive up to a 9-month grace period. 
 Cosigner release 
 Cosigner release requirements vary by Splash lending partner. In most cases, you can request a cosigner release after a year of consecutive, on-time loan payments (12 in total). Once the lender evaluates and approves the borrower's finances and creditworthiness, the lender will release the cosigner. However, this varies by lender, so read the terms and conditions of your specific loan closely. 
 Eligibility requirements 
 Credit score 
 Splash Financial recommends a credit score of 680 or higher to qualify for a loan with its lenders. However, you may still qualify for a loan with a lower rate. 
 Income requirements 
 Eligibility requirements vary by lender. For student loans, income requirements vary, but a cosigner's income can improve your chances of qualifying and secure better interest rates. 
 For student loan refinancing, lenders typically look for a low debt-to-income ratio (less than 30%), a strong credit score and a history of on-time payments. Other eligibility criteria may include whether you graduated, a minimum income level and whether you are a permanent U.S. resident or citizen. 
 Cosigner requirements 
 A cosigner needs a credit score of 680 or higher. Other factors, like income requirements, stable income and citizenship, vary by Splash loan partner. 
 School eligibility 
 Splash Financial is an independent loan marketplace that helps you find and secure a student loan. This provider doesn't have a specific list of accepted schools. Instead, you'll need to submit your school information with each lender that you want a quote from. 
 Application process 
 Start by completing Splash Financial's 3-minute online application with your school, name and contact information. This application then takes you to Splash Financial's partner website to fill out the remaining questions specific to that lender. 
 Once you fill out the application, Splash conducts a soft credit pull to give you pre-qualified rates. This won't affect your credit score and is used for rate accuracy. Then, you'll be asked to submit documentation, such as your ID and a pay stub to verify your income, but this varies based on the lending partner. 
 After selecting a lender, you'll submit an application to the lending partner, which will complete a hard credit inquiry to verify your identity and application information. This process appears on your credit report and may impact your credit score. 
 Get started with Splash Financial 
 Customer experience 
 Customer support 
 You can reach Splash Financial's customer service at (800)-349-3938 Monday through Friday, 9 am to 9 pm EST. You can also contact it by emailing contact@splashfinancial.com or using the built-in chat feature on its website. 
 Website 
 Our team doesn't love Splash Financial's website. While visually appealing, the website hid key information, such as repayment terms, loan interest rates and origination fees, in the terms and conditions in fine print at the bottom of the website. This made it challenging to get a clear idea of the potential interest rates you could end up with, as the main website highlights only the low interest rates — but not the full interest range or fees that could be tacked on. 
 Customer reviews 
 Splash Financial has an excellent 4.8-star rating from over 2,500 Trustpilot reviews, with many noting that the provider made the loan application or refinancing process hassle-free and quick. Positive reviews highlight the easy application process and consistent, informative customer service. In contrast, negative reviews often note that the loan money takes longer than expected to deposit or reach the right recipient, and some shared that interest rates are higher than other marketplaces. 
 Splash Financial pros and cons 
 Pros: 
 Doesn't impact your credit score when checking rates 
 Quick eligibility check 
 Skip-a-payment option available once per year for graduate students via some lenders 
 Cons 
 Higher credit score requirements than some lenders 
 Checking rates requires going to each lender's website 
 Expensive origination fee with some lenders (up to 15%)

 Is Splash Financial right for you? 
 Splash Financial may be the right fit for the following borrowers: 
 Borrowers who need quick loan turnaround times 
 Those with good to excellent credit 
 Students applying with a cosigner 
 Graduate students who need to take out loans (Splash lenders offer several graduate-specific benefits and promotions) 
 Bottom line 
 Splash Financial's straightforward process can save borrowers and their families a lot of time finding and securing private student loans. You can quickly compare lenders with only a soft-credit pull, which won't harm your credit score. Overall, this marketplace is worth checking out if you want to see what you pre-qualify for, but keep in mind you may be charged an origination fee in some cases. 
 FAQs 
 Is Splash Financial a legit company? 
 Yes, Splash Financial is a legit company with an A+ BBB rating, accreditation and strong customer reviews. You can check your rates through this provider's quick pre-qualification process at no cost. 
 Is Splash Financial the same as SoFi? 
 No, Splash Financial is a private loan marketplace that connects you with lenders, while SoFi is a direct lender and bank that directly lends money to borrowers. 
 Does Splash Financial offer student loan refinancing? 
 Yes, Splash Financial offers student loan refinancing for loans with a minimum balance of $5,000, typically.
